rmd.publication: 2025 Publication 590-B; HTML examples explicitly calculate 2026 distributions
rmd.official_csv_json: No official CSV/JSON found. Official HTML has complete numeric tables suitable for deterministic extraction; not necessary to rely on third-party files.
rmd.table_location: Appendix B. Table II (Joint and Last Survivor Life Expectancy), web text lines2846-3558 approximately; Table III lines3559-3591.
extraction_recipe: Fetch official HTML through authorized network/browser capability.
Find Appendix B Table II and stop at Table III; tables are split into continued blocks, with Ages row defining each column-age group.
Parse row age and each numeric cell against current Ages header. Do not mistake continued repeated headers for values.
Use pair min(age1,age2),max(age1,age2) or symmetric mapping; verify same pair has identical repeated value.
Retain exact one-decimal numeric factors and publication version/source/hash, never extrapolate factors from Uniform table.
Check expected age coverage and report missing cells rather than filling guesses; special 120-and-over labels need explicit clamping only as official table instructs.
Commit extracted local data for runtime automatic lookup; expose age and beneficiary inputs, not manual distribution factor.
rmd.network_status: Official HTML accessible via web tool; direct shell urllib public fetch denied Operation not permitted. No network workaround attempted. Full numeric matrix not saved; web view returned limited windows.
rmd.table_selection: Table II only when spouse is sole beneficiary AND spouse more than ten years younger. Otherwise Table III for living owner. Table I concerns beneficiaries and is not a substitute.
rmd.age_basis: Each person's attained age on birthday in distribution year. Balance prior Dec31. Recompute joint factor yearly using both attained ages.
rmd.formula: RMD=prior_Dec31_balance/table_factor; projected ending balance=B*(1+annual_return)-RMD for year-end distribution.

starting_age_rules.note: Historical exact birth date required; birth year alone cannot distinguish1949 cohorts.

starting_age_rules.legal_status: 2024 final regulations reserved this cohort due SECURE2.0 drafting ambiguity; companion proposed REG-103529-23 specifies73. Verify any later finalization before release. Old IRS2023 training slide says75 and is superseded for planning purposes.

rmd.deadlines: First year's RMD may be delayed to April1 of following year; later RMDs due Dec31, so deferral can create two payments next year. IRA owner still employed has no retirement deferral; workplace plan may permit later-of-retirement unless5% owner. Roth owner generally exempt, inherited-account rules separate. 2020 CARES waiver requires historical handling.
limits: Complete TableII extraction remains required for supported age grid.
Pre2022 historical RMD uses older factors; current factor table cannot silently serve historical years.
Original UI primary beneficiary wording is less strict than official sole beneficiary rule; implement accurate sole-beneficiary wording.

ssa.early_formula: For k months before FRA, benefit factor=1-min(k,36)*(5/9)/100-max(k-36,0)*(5/12)/100. This is worker retirement benefit; spousal/survivor formulas differ.
ssa.delayed_formula: For d months after FRA through month before70, factor=1+d*(annual_delayed_credit/12). Credits are additive to PIA, not compound growth. Born>=1943 annual credit8%. No additional credit after70.
timing_caveats: SSA benefits generally paid in month following effective month.
January1 DOB uses prior year for delayed-credit table; first-of-month DOB treated previous month for FRA.
Before age70 some credits apply in January after benefits begin; SSA comparison calculator applies all credits for comparison.

reference_modes.meaning: Optimize claiming age62-70 using normalized benefit base; no salary or earnings history fields, so cannot estimate dollar entitlement.
reference_modes.proposed_model: For each candidate claim month/age, apply SSA factor to a common PIA base and compound monthly benefit cash flows to life expectancy; choose max terminal value (equivalent common-date PV ranking).
unknowns: Whether original searches integer years or months
Whether base is$1000 or another normalization
Original COLA base date and step timing
Whether original compares undiscounted totals or investment-adjusted terminal wealth: financial-return input implies adjustment but not observed by submission

reference_modes.meaning: Use user-entered monthly benefits, not rederive them from SSA factors.
reference_modes.proposed_model: Monthly stream simulation from earlier claim through horizon; calculate cumulative nominal and investment-adjusted balances and first breakeven. Allow never-crossing result.

ssa.limits: Independent mathematically grounded model can be implemented, but source-parity remains unverified until actual original result submissions are compared. Do not claim exact parity from explanatory prose alone.
